text:
anya: Quick question for the group — we need a concise guideline on what to include in the quant calibration dataset for the FP8/INT8 rollout. Thoughts?

matt: short answer: mixes of seq lengths + warmups. we saw weird regressions on long-context tails when we only used short examples.

sophia: agree. also include KV-warmup sequences that mimic chat prefixes. if KV-cache patterns aren't represented the per-token latency/accuracy trade-offs shift.

raj: are we converging on per-channel or per-tensor for weights? per-channel helped on MLPs but increased kernel divergence in some layers.

matt: empirical from last profile: per-channel reduced quantization error (avg logit KL down ~0.12) but caused more kernel variants to be selected at runtime — ~8% extra kernel-switch overhead on the 80B path.

lucas: that kernel switching tax matters for small batches. for our p50 latency SLAs, that ~8% bump translated to missing the SLO in a couple of p95 workloads.

anya: so tradeoff: better numeric fidelity vs more runtime complexity. For rollout, maybe pick per-tensor for narrow-latency SLO customers and per-channel for Dedicated where throughput matters?

sophia: Also we need to define outlier handling rules. Last run, generous clipping at 99.9 percentile fixed a few hallucination cases. but it also clipped rare-but-legit tokens.

matt: proposal: two-stage pipeline — 1) run 10k samples to detect weight-wise outliers (per-channel statistics), 2) cap extreme activations with a conservative percentile (e.g., 99.995) but keep an allowlist for tokens/positions seen in prod.

anya: how about dataset composition? percentages?

sophia: suggested mix: 60% short interactive turns (<=64), 30% medium (65-512), 10% long (512+). additionally include ~5% adversarial prompts (triggers for rare tokens).

raj: want to add traffic-sampled slices — i.e., top-1000 most common prefixes from prod, and tail-1000 rare-but-critical prefixes. That helps calibration reflect both OOD and common.

lucas: important: include batching/concat artifacts. our profiler showed that concat batching changes KV layout and increased quant error marginally. include examples where several short messages are concatenated.

anya: can someone draft the sampling command we can run in CI for dataset generation?

matt: draft command (pseudo):
```
python tools/sample_calib.py \
  --output calib/2026-03-18.npz \
  --seed 42 \
  --mix "short:0.6,medium:0.3,long:0.1" \
  --include-warmups true \
  --traffic-sample top1000,tail1000 \
  --adversarial-percent 0.05 \
  --max-samples 10000
```

sophia: add a flag to keep original tokenization so we can reproduce per-subtoken distributions. and log sequence-len histogram.

raj: metrics to capture post-quant: KL on logits, MSE on embedding outputs, end-to-end decoding BLEU-like score for targeted evals, and perf: tokens/sec and kernel-switch counts.

lucas: also capture KV-cache hit profile: measure prefix reuse ratio. we found that datasets without high prefix reuse underrepresent KVCACHE warmup perf gains.

ci-bot: CI check queued: quant-dataset-gen // see run 5342 for downstream tests.

anya: plan: sophia + matt to produce the generator and vet the first dataset. raj/lucas will run perf + kernel-selection profiling. we'll reconvene after first pass (T+3 days). @sophia @matt please ping here when ready. :thumbsup:

matt: noted. I'll start the sampler and include a small run to compare per-channel vs per-tensor on the 7B/13B/70B quant banks. will post profiler snapshots.

sophia: I'll add adversarial seed list and traffic slices. aiming for reproducible manifest + hashes.

anya: perfect — thanks team. keep notes about any regression-causing samples so we can triage dataset-induced perf regressions.

lucas: one last note: record hardware and kernel versions in the dataset manifest (cuda/driver/torch/llvm/kernels) — kernel selection behavior changed across minor driver bumps.

anya: agreed. adding that to the manifest requirements.

matt: FYI preliminary numbers earlier: INT8 median speedup 1.9x vs fp16, FP8 ~2.4x but with 1.2% higher logit KL on average for long tails. exacts will change by model/arch.

anya: ok closing — will create a short checklist doc from this thread and link it into the rollout playbook.
